statements.details: Both images ship the same binary with github.com/gorilla/websocket v1.5.1. The weak client-frame mask-key implementation is not present: v1.5.1 initializes maskRand from crypto/rand.Reader. Containd only uses websocket.Upgrader as a server for the authenticated, single-use-ticket /api/v1/cli/ws endpoint (api/http/cli_handlers.go and api/http/server.go); server writes do not generate masks.
statements.threat: The advisory concerns predictable client-frame mask keys. Govulncheck v1.9.0 reports broad websocket symbols (GO-2026-6278), including server methods, as reachable. Source inspection of v1.5.1 conn.go shows crypto/rand mask generation and the !isServer guard on mask generation. Containd does not create WebSocket clients; the scanner version match does not establish vulnerable mask generation.

statements.details: GO-2026-6860 affects golang.org/x/net/html Parse/ParseFragment and parser.addText/fosterParent. Containd directly uses x/net for network diagnostics; its mimetype dependency also imports html tokenization for charset detection. The affected parser/renderer code is not linked into either image binary. Linux amd64 and arm64 govulncheck v1.9.0 symbol-level analysis finds module/package matches but no affected-symbol call traces; symbol tables confirm the affected parser/renderer symbols are absent.
statements.threat: The presence of the x/net module and HTML tokenizer does not make the affected HTML tree parser or renderer present. The transitive import is github.com/gabriel-vasile/mimetype/internal/charset, which uses html.NewTokenizer, not the affected parsing/rendering APIs.

statements.details: Containd uses golang.org/x/crypto for SSH and bcrypt, not OpenPGP. Neither the direct nor transitive Linux dependency graph imports golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp or its subpackages. Govulncheck v1.9.0 symbol-level analysis reports only a module match; both architecture symbol tables contain no OpenPGP code.
statements.threat: The unmaintained OpenPGP implementation is not linked into the shared containd binary in either image. The x/crypto module version alone is not evidence of OpenPGP exposure.

statements.details: The ZIP parser in Wolfi clamav-1.5 1.5.2-r7 is affected (secdb fixed version 1.5.4-r2). Both release images contain this package. The management image defaults to combined mode; the standalone engine also runs the AV owner, supervises clamd/FreshClam and serves the HTTP scanning gate (pkg/app/engine/engine.go). With AV enabled in ClamAV mode and HTTP upload or download scanning enabled, complete HTTP bodies reach clamd via INSTREAM (pkg/dp/httpgate/transaction.go, response.go; pkg/cp/services/av_scan.go and clamav.go).
statements.threat: Adversary-controlled HTTP upload/download bodies can reach the affected ZIP parser when ClamAV-mode HTTP scanning is enabled. Engine-only deployment does not remove this exposure: the engine owns both the gate and clamd. AV disabled or ICAP mode does not send these HTTP objects to the local ClamAV parser.

remediations.details: Disable ClamAV-mode HTTP upload and download scanning (or disable AV), or use ICAP mode with an independently maintained scanner, until a fixed containd image ships. Disabling scanning removes this inspection protection; assess the resulting policy exposure.

No fixed containd image is available for this finding. As checked on 2026-11-05, Wolfi secdb lists clamav-1.5 1.5.4-r2 as fixed, but the x86_64 and aarch64 package indexes publish only versions through 1.5.2-r7. A secdb fixed-version entry is not an available image update.

statements.details: *sshole affects OpenSSH's non-PAM Unix password authentication on musl, where crypt() returns "*" for an overlong password and matches a stored "*" password field. Containd ships no OpenSSH, dropbear or libssh. Its SSH service is the Go golang.org/x/crypto/ssh server in pkg/mp/sshserver, whose password callback checks containd's own user store with bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword and never reads /etc/shadow or calls crypt(). The binaries are built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and the runtime base is Wolfi (glibc).
